extracted.intended_audience: licensed customs brokers, brokeraging firms, continuing education providers, prospective accreditors, and CBP stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule and implementing requirements establishing a continuing broker education program for active individual customs broker license holders, including credit requirements, qualifying activities, accreditation, recordkeeping, notification, enforcement, and economic assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 36 hours per three-year reporting period requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule requires active individual customs broker license holders to complete 36 hours of continuing education every three years, in line with the triennial status reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to increase broker knowledge, educate on changing customs requirements, reduce errors and penalties, and professionalize the broker community. First certification of compliance is due when filing the 2027 triennial status report; brokers licensed mid-period may be prorated or exempt for the first triennial report as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying continuing broker education activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying activities include attending or presenting at accredited events, such as courses, seminars, symposia, and conventions; online activities, including qualified trainings provided in-house; and self-guided online modules (with conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-guided, online courses or content are acceptable if accredited and culminate in a retention test. CBP clarifies that online activities and in-house trainings can qualify. No minimum subject-matter requirements are imposed by this rule, though CBP believes PGA-related courses are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of half credits (30-minute units)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP recognizes half credits for 30 minutes of continuing broker education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This modification to the NPRM clarifies credit granularity so shorter qualifying activities can yield fractional credit toward the 36-hour requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-attestation on triennial status report (no attachment required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers are required to self-attest to the completion of the required continuing broker education on each triennial status report and will not be required to input or attach evidence of the 36 continuing education credits with their triennial status reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brokers must maintain records and produce them only if CBP requests them under §111.102(d)(2). The triennial self-certification is the reporting mechanism; documentation is retained by the broker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping content and retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers must maintain records consisting of certain documentation received from the provider or host of the qualifying continuing broker education containing information pertaining to the dates, titles, providers, credit hours earned, and location (if applicable) for each training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records can be in any format (electronically or on paper). CBP has authority to request records for a period of three years following the submission of the status report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation by CBP-designated accreditors
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will designate entities outside of CBP to act as accreditors for qualifying continuing broker education after an application process (via RFP released every three years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential accreditors submit applications detailing their standards for accreditation, quality control practices, application process, and other information. A panel of CBP experts will review and approve or deny applications. Once approved, accreditors accept submissions from program creators or companies seeking accreditation for specific programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor renewal/application cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP anticipates releasing, every three years, an RFP soliciting applications to become an accreditor; every three years following the first cycle, existing accreditors will also apply for renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a recurring review and renewal cadence for accreditors to maintain oversight and quality control over accredited offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor responsibilities and credit determination
rubrics_metrics.description: An accreditor is responsible for reviewing course content and determining the number of credits or hours to be granted for each course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditors should have standards and quality control practices; their determinations establish which offerings qualify and how many continuing education credits they provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government agency training exemption from accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Training or educational activities offered by U.S. government agencies—so long as the content is relevant to customs business as identified by CBP in coordination with the offering agency—do not require accreditation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will identify, in coordination with other U.S. government agencies when applicable, qualified continuing broker education offered by a government agency that is relevant to customs business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification procedures and broker contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will send notifications to an individual broker's email address, if an email address is on file, otherwise to an individual broker's physical address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP declined to require an automated warning when status reports are incomplete; brokers may verify/update contact information in the ACE Portal to ensure correct delivery. CBP cannot guarantee the eCBP Portal will flag missing fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement thresholds, timelines, and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual broker files an incomplete triennial status report by failing to certify compliance, a 30-day timeframe to respond is triggered; failure may lead to license suspension under §111.104(c). If suspended, the broker can take corrective action on or before 120 calendar days from the date of issuance of the order of suspension to avoid revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP views certifying completion as essential to maintaining an active license. Corrective action can range from certifying completion of the requirement to completing 36 continuing education credits. CBP considers 30 days and 120 days to be sufficient and prefers universally applied timeframes to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule applies to any individual holding an active customs broker license. Individual brokers who have voluntarily suspended their licenses are not required to complete continuing broker education until they elect to reactivate their licenses (pro-rated depending upon timing). Individual brokers who have not held their license for an entire triennial period at the time their first triennial status report is due are exempted from completing training and reporting in their first triennial status report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of 2022, CBP estimates 13,952 active individual brokers; compliance schedules and projections are specified for cohorts licensed in different years (first certifications due with 2027 triennial status reports and later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider and accreditor application pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers of continuing broker education must apply to accreditors to have their coursework certified; accreditors (once designated) accept submissions from program creators or companies seeking accreditation for specific programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditors will review provider submissions and determine qualification and crediting. Content providers may apply to multiple accreditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis assumptions used to assess costs and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP's economic analysis estimates costs and benefits to brokers, accreditors, providers, and CBP; key assumptions include time spent researching/registering (approx. 3 hours per triennial period), average loaded wage rate of $34.81, and average hourly monetary cost of trainings ranging from $0 (low) to $30 (medium) to $50 (high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP assumes varying broker behaviors: low-cost (free trainings), medium-cost (mix with one major conference/year), and high-cost (all paid, two conferences/year). Based on these assumptions CBP estimates per-credit and aggregate costs and projection of affected brokers (assumes ~60% already in compliance). These assumptions were not commented on in the NPRM and are used to calculate estimated costs over the period of analysis.
